title: Conditional Support for AI Assisted Environmental Business Compliance in Bangladesh
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) may help businesses identify environmental obligations, yet support for its use can depend on how a proposed service is governed. This cross-sectional study distinguishes perceived usefulness for identifying obligations from support conditional on transparency and accountability. It uses 385 adult responses to a common questionnaire on AI, environment and climate justice in Bangladesh. We report individual item distributions, joint endorsement and paired comparisons, followed by exploratory adjusted models of conditional support and expected consistency of compliance practices. Conditional support was endorsed by 315 respondents (81.8%), whereas 230 (59.7%) endorsed usefulness for identifying obligations. The paired difference was 22.1 percentage points (95% CI 15.8 to 28.1; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Both were endorsed by 189 respondents (49.1%). Of the 315 conditional supporters, 116 also endorsed both updating tools when relevant rules change and retaining human legal review for complex decisions. No focal adjusted coefficient met the multiplicity-adjusted threshold. The findings distinguish support for a stated governance condition from endorsement of a specific task and show why a single acceptance score would obscure the response patterns. They motivate separate evaluation of rule currency, human review and practical usefulness when assessing compliance tools. The study measures stated judgements in a mixed adult sample; it does not estimate the effect of safeguards on uptake, verify compliance or observe enforcement outcomes.
